newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says Brazil interested in Shell's Camisea gas.
newsitem.headline: Peru says Brazil interested in Shell's Camisea gas.

text.p: Peru said Thursday Brazil was interested in receiving a liquid natural gas supply from the huge Camisea reserves being developed by the Anglo-Dutch Royal Dutch/Shell group.

Brazil's Mines and Energy Minister Raimundo Mendes de Brito told his Peruvian counterpart Alberto Pandolfi at a recent meeting that his country would also be interested in a supply of ethane from Camisea, government daily El Peruano reported.

Shell, which is halfway through a two year license to explore the reserves -- estimated to hold 11 trillion cubic feet of natural gas and 600 million barrels of natural gas liquids -- hopes to transport gas to Peru's Pacific coast by late 2001.
With a gas bonanza expected on the back of its Camisea project, Shell has not ruled out any supply options. But it has made no plans to supply Brazil, according to company officials.
Earlier this month, Shell said extracting ethane from the reserves was possible but would need a $1 billion investment to build an ethylene plant.
